description: Ask a Jury helps with anonymous personal dilemmas. Six real human jurors — not AI personas — privately vote on cases you submit on askajury.com. ChatGPT can explain how it works and, after you approve the exact wording, prepare a temporary one-hour draft link. You open the link, sign in if needed, review, and submit yourself. ChatGPT never posts a live case, votes, or issues a verdict.

defaultPrompt: My roommate keeps using my stuff without asking. I'd like to hear what real people think about how I should handle it.
How does Ask a Jury work, and when should I use it instead of asking ChatGPT?
I'm torn about a relationship situation — can I get opinions from actual humans, not AI?
